page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Pulling out the stops
title: Pulling out the stops
topic: Language for getting things done quickly
description:
There's much to do at the offices of Tip Top Trading, and tomorrow the team is launching its new product – the plastic aubergine. So everyone needs to pull their weight and get things done quickly. The problem is, some people are a bit slow at being quick!
This episode focuses on the language that you might use when trying to get your team to do something quickly and under pressure.
phrases: We've got to pull out all the stops.
We have an order we need to process urgently.
We need to pull out all the stops to get this sorted.
This is our number one priority.

listening_challenge.question: What has Anna made her number one priority?
listening_challenge.answer: To get the grapes to Nice'n'Cheesy.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: It's that time again for English at Work. Life in the offices of Tip Top Trading is still hectic. There's so much to do and tomorrow the team is launching its new product – the plastic aubergine – so everyone needs to pull their weight and get things done – quickly. The problem is, some people are a bit slow at being quick!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Could someone answer that please? I'm on the other line.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Well I can't, I'm already on the phone.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah, talking to your friend Marge. And I'm busy… errr… writing a business proposal.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Could someone just answer that phone… oh, you're all busy. I suppose I'd better do it. Hello? Yes? Really! I'm sorry about that. We'll send someone round right away. Yes, this morning. Bye. Anna, are you free to talk in my office now?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes Paul. What's wrong?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Hold on – I just need a quick bite on a biscuit – that's better. Now, that was Nice'n'Cheesy. They're not happy about how slowly we are processing their order. They need our plastic grapes for an exhibition they're doing at the weekend.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: But I thought Tom had sorted that out?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Clearly not. I need you to pull out all the stops and sort this out.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Pull out what stops?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: I mean do all you can to get this order completed, please.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: But we've got the aubergine launch tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Leave that to me and Denise to organise. It'll be in… safe hands.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hmm, I'm not so sure about that. Anyway Anna, your priority now is the order for Nice'n'Cheesy. You're going to have to tell the team "We have an order we need to process urgently", and "We need to pull out all the stops to get this sorted". You could also say "This is our number one priority" and then delegate tasks to the team to help you get the order sorted. Good luck!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh thanks. Tom, I need your help. It's the order for Nice'n'Cheesy, we need to process it urgently.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: The order? I sent that out ages ago, with the paperwork.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: You mean this paperwork Tom, on your desk?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh no! I must have forgotten. I've had so much to do.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, they're not happy, so we've got to pull out all the stops and get them their grapes.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: OK but what about the aubergines?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Forget about the aubergines. We've got to get onto this now. It's our number one priority. You go and get the plastic grapes from the warehouse, I'll sort out this paperwork, and I'll meet you downstairs in 15 minutes.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Why, where are we going?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: We're getting a taxi to the offices of Nice'n'Cheesy so we can hand deliver the grapes.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh right, but isn't it nearly lunchtime?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: There's no time for lunch, Tom. We need to do this now!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh Anna, you're amazing.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: She certainly is! Anna has wasted no time in sorting out this problem and that's important if you want to keep your business going. Here's a reminder of some of the phrases Anna used:
We've got to pull out all the stops.
We have an order we need to process urgently.
We need to pull out all the stops to get this sorted.
This is our number one priority.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Tom and Anna have made it to the offices of Nice'n'Cheesy. Let's find out how they're getting on.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: …so we're really sorry…

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah, really sorry…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: …about the delay, and it won't happen again. And we hope you're pleased with the grapes…

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: …and the price!

transcript.speaker: Jane
transcript.text: Yes, the price is very competitive and if you can guarantee a bit more 'customer care', then I'm sure we'll be buying from you again.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes, of course. Thanks very much and sorry again. We hope to see you again soon. Bye!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah, yeah, see you.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Phew, well done Anna. I think you saved the day once again. Hey, hold on, isn't that your boyfriend, Dave from IT, over there?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: It is. But who's he with?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: You mean, who's he holding hands with? It's Julie from accounts!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No, it can't be… It is! What's Dave doing with another woman?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I dunno – but I never trusted him. Come on Anna, you need a drink – a big one.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Oh dear. Poor Anna, it looks like Dave's been cheating on her, but she needs to keep a clear head for the big launch of the plastic aubergine tomorrow. Will she be led by her head - or her heart? Find out next time on English at Work. Bye!
